services.name: Blotato Engine
services.tagline: Unified social API, MCP server and full web console for 9 platforms. Self-hosted, unlimited posts, zero subscription.
services.summary: Blotato sells a unified social media API and MCP server for $29/mo. This engine reproduces the whole surface — publishing, scheduling, comments, DMs, keyword automations, analytics, visual generation and source repurposing — across 38 REST endpoints and 17 MCP tools, plus a nine-screen web console. Same request shapes, same tool names, no per-seat billing and no post caps.
highlights: 38 REST endpoints covering every Blotato capability area
17 MCP tools so Claude, Cursor and Hermes drive it directly
Nine-screen web console served from the same origin — no build step
Nine platform connectors; the four newest talk to real platform APIs
Background scheduler plus recurring weekly slot calendar
Keyword DM automations with gates, webhook callbacks and run stats
Visual renderer producing real PNGs from six templates

features.title: Publishing
features.body: One POST /v2/posts targets any connected account. The connector registry resolves the platform adapter from the account record, so adding a platform never touches client code.

features.title: Scheduling
features.body: Pass an ISO-8601 scheduledTime and the APScheduler worker dispatches within 15 seconds of the due time. Recurring weekly slots per account, plus next-free-slot resolution in the account timezone.

features.title: Comments and DMs
features.body: Read comments, reply publicly, list DM threads with unread counts, read transcripts and send outbound messages. Everything the agent needs to handle its own follow-up.

features.title: DM automations
features.body: Keyword triggers on comments or messages. On a hit the engine posts a randomized public reply, sends the DM, applies follow or email gates, and fires your webhook. Meta's callback shape is handled at /webhooks/meta.

features.title: Analytics
features.body: Snapshot history per post, aggregate totals, engagement rate, and top-post ranking by views, likes, comments, shares, saves or reach.

features.title: Visuals
features.body: Six templates render actual PNGs with Pillow: quote cards, tweet cards, 4:5 carousels, whiteboard and chalkboard infographics, and tutorial carousels. Outputs are served back as public URLs.

features.title: Sources
features.body: Feed it a YouTube link, article, PDF, X post or raw text. It extracts the content and repurposes it into platform-shaped drafts ready for the composer.

features.title: Web console
features.body: A nine-screen dashboard: overview, composer with fan-out publishing, queue and slot calendar, inbox, automations, visual studio, sources, analytics and settings. Vanilla JS, one file, no build step.

ui.intro: The console is served at / from the same process as the API, so there is nothing to deploy separately. It authenticates with the same API key and keeps it in browser storage.

usage.title: Build a keyword DM automation
usage.desc: Comment triggers a public reply variant plus a direct message. Test it without a real comment.
usage.code:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8400/v2/dm-automations \
  -H "blotato-api-key: $BLOTATO_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "<ACCOUNT_ID>",
    "name": "Price keyword",
    "dmMessage": "Here is the link you asked for.",
    "triggers": [{"type":"comment-received","keywords":["price"],"isActive":true}],
    "commentReply": {"variants": [
      {"text":"Sent you a DM {{mention}}"},
      {"text":"Check your inbox {{mention}}"},
      {"text":"DM sent {{mention}}"}
    ]}
  }'

curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8400/v2/dm-automations/<ID>/test \
  -H "blotato-api-key: $BLOTATO_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"what is the price?","author":"tester"}'

usage.title: Connect an agent over MCP
usage.desc: Any MCP-capable agent that connects gets all 17 tools with no extra wiring.

uv run python scripts/create_api_key.py \
  --client "Acme Agency" \
  --plan starter \
  --credits 1000

notes: Credentials are strict on purpose. If you supply real credentials and they are incomplete or rejected, the post fails with the platform's own error. The engine never reports a fake publish. Responses carry a `simulated` flag so demo output is always distinguishable from live output.
Publishing to real platforms needs approved developer apps. Meta needs instagram_content_publish and pages_manage_posts; X needs a paid write tier; TikTok needs content posting access.
Accounts seeded with provider "mock" publish through a deterministic simulator. That keeps the whole pipeline testable before app review, and every simulated post is labelled.
Media must be publicly reachable URLs for platform APIs. Use POST /v2/media/upload to host it locally, then expose the service behind TLS.
SQLite is the default store. For multi-instance deployments switch DATABASE_URL to Postgres.
Never expose port 8400 directly. Put it behind Nginx or Caddy with TLS before selling access, and change MASTER_API_KEY.
The web console ships in static/ with no build step. If you rebrand it, keep the api-key header name or the engine will reject requests.

faq.q: Is this the same API as Blotato?
faq.a: The request shapes, endpoint paths and MCP tool names intentionally match, so existing n8n flows and agent prompts work unchanged. Blotato's hosted service is a separate product; this is an independent implementation you run yourself.

faq.q: Does it really render carousels and infographics?
faq.a: Yes. Six templates render PNGs with Pillow at 1080x1080 or 1080x1350 and are served back as public URLs. The test suite asserts a real file lands on disk above a size threshold.

faq.q: Can I sell access to it?
faq.a: Yes. Keys carry plans and credit balances, and the API refuses writes once a key is exhausted. Mint keys with scripts/create_api_key.py, collect payment however you like, top up the balance when they renew.

faq.q: How do DM automations get triggered in production?
faq.a: Point your Meta app's webhook at /webhooks/meta. The engine parses comment and message events, matches keywords, posts the reply variant, sends the DM and fires your own webhook. For other platforms or custom logic, POST to /webhooks/test with the same event shape.
The registry falls back to a deterministic mock adapter that returns a plausible URL and status. That keeps the pipeline testable before you have app review approval.
